MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 24, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at
5:00 p.m., on June 24, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 19, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9 Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v. Mission Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-
  01376969-CU-MC-CJC

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators - Property: 25282 Marguerite Parkway,
  Mission Viejo, Ca 92692; Agency Negotiators: City Manager Elaine Lister, Assistant
  City Manager Jerry Hill, City Attorney William P. Curley III, Director of
  Administrative Services/City Treasurer Ellis Chang. Negotiation Parties: Kathleen
  Sickles, Property Representative. Under negotiation: terms of payment.

City Council Minutes  1  June 24, 2025
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 Mayor Ruesch recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:00 Mayor Ruesch
reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley stated there were two closed session items that the Council was updated, but
no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ruesch

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club on Receiving the "2024 Golf Course of the Year"
  Award by the California Golf Course Owners Association

  Presented commendation to General Manager Matthew Donovan.

P2. Recognize Crime Prevention Specialist Lisa LeBron-Flores for Receiving the "OCSD
  Sheriff 2024 Civilian Employee of the Year" Award

  Present commendation to Lisa LeBron-Flores

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Carolyn Gatto M.V.: Spoke on an incident with a deputy issuing a ticket to one of the protestors
who stopped her car by the bus shelter to unload signs for the rally. She feels this was a politically
motivated act and that the deputy could have given the driver a warning. She reminded the Council
and Sheriff’s department that she had asked for police protection during the protests. She made a
point that the rallies will not stop, and they will continue to be held every Wednesday from 11 to 1.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke on future planning for affordable housing and indicated that the City has
several sights that could be used and has chosen not to. He asked if the City could provide stools in
the hallway for the deputies that are at the council meetings.

Rich Pullium, M.V.: Thanked the City Council and city staff for all they did. Asked that the
invocation be removed from the meetings. Spoke on the Pride event this past Saturday and thanked
Council Member Vasquez for attending. Asked hypothetical question regarding ICE and asked
what the policy is in the City.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Addressed the item regarding the fuel reduction project criticizing the
bidding process and spoke out on West Coast Arborists amendments.

City Council Minutes  2  June 24, 2025
 Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Asked for a litigation update on the Los Oso project. Asked for more clarity
on motions in the future. Make it clear that she was not lobbying to defend the Library in her
comments from the last meeting.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Spoke on an ice raid in Santa Ana and spoke out on Trump’s policies
regarding minorities.

Chris Perko, M.V.: Spoke on all the Pride displays at various states that she visited and feels very
let down that the City does not participate in Pride month.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
consent calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 10, 2025, as presented.

2.  Golf Check Register Dated May 30, 2025, in the Amount of $10,341.49

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated May 30, 2025, in the Amount of $1,104,693.12

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  General Check Register Dated June 6, 2025, in the Amount of $1,524,567.53

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated June 6, 2025, in the Amount of $32,772.10

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  FY 2025/26 Budget for the Mission Viejo Housing Authority

  Adopted HA Resolution 25-01 Adopting a Budget for the 2025/26 Fiscal Year.

City Council Minutes  3  June 24, 2025
 7.  FY 2025/26 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 25-01 Adopting Budget for the 2025/26 Fiscal Year.

8.  Fifth Asset dba Debtbook’s Lease and SBITA Management Software-as-a-Service
  (SaaS) Application

  Approved procurement of Debtbook's Lease (A25-25) and SBITA Management SaaS
  Application, pending adoption of the 2025-27 Proposed Budget for an initial term of three
  years, with ongoing annual options to renew.

9.  Olympiad Road/Felipe Road Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP
  24258)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Crosstown Electrical & Data, Inc.
  (A25-22) in the amount of $435,437.50.

10. 2024 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 25838)-Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk to
  record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation
  of the Notice of Completion.

11. Mission Viejo Fuel Reduction Project - CalFire Grant

  (1) Awarded contract for the Mission Viejo Fuel Reduction Project - CalFire Grant to West
  Coast Arborists, Inc. (A25-23) for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 in the
  amount of $1,830,000.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order for the Mission
  Viejo Fuel Reduction Project to West Coast Arborists, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2025
  through June 30, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $1,000,000.00 pending adoption of the
  2025-2027 budget by City Council.

12. Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2025 - Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 25-25 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on
  Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council to
  Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing Protests;
  (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds in
  accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instructed the City Clerk to
  set the Public Hearing for August 26, 2025.

13. Oso Creek Golf Course - Purchase of Replacement Fairway Reelmaster Mower

City Council Minutes  4  June 24, 2025
   (1) Approved purchase for the replacement of the Oso Creek Golf Course fairway Reelmaster
  Mower to Turf Star Western, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $102,736.70; and (2) authorized
  staff to issue a purchase order to Turf Star Western, Inc. for a not to exceed amount of
  $102,736.70.

14. Annual Routine Landscape and Irrigation Supplies

  (1) Approved Tenth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with SiteOne
  Landscape Supply and (2) authorized issuance of a change order to the existing Purchase
  Order for Landscape and Irrigation Supplies to SiteOne Landscape Supply in an amount not
  to exceed $15,000.00.

15. Annual Routine Monthly Landscape Maintenance - Contract Area 8

  (1) Approved Seventh Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Nieves
  Landscape, LLC, and (2) authorized the issuance of a change order to the existing Purchase
  Order for Landscape Contract Area 8 to Nieves Landscape, Inc. in an amount not to exceed
  $70,000.00.

16. Legislative Advocacy and Government Relations Services

  Approved the Professional Services Agreement with Townsend Public Affairs, Inc.(A25-24)
  for State legislative advocacy and government relations services for a total not to exceed the
  amount of $156,000 for the period of July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027.

OLD BUSINESS

17. Adoption of the 2025-2027 Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Ellis Chang presented the staff report.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Echoed Cathy Palmer’s comments regarding the $3,500 for the marine
  welcome packages. Voiced his concerns about the proposed parking structure at the Oso
  Viejo Golf Course and the lack of connection between the golf course and the urban core. He
  expressed from a planning standpoint of view that the City could do a lot better by developing
  a specific plan.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: Stated that the most precious assets are the employees that work for the
  City. He thanked the Council for the approval of the salary schedule, performance merit
  increases, COLA, and bonuses. He urged the Council to adopt the budget as presented.

  Council Member Vasquez stated it was her understanding that the additional $3,500 Council
  Member Kelley asked for the Marine Adoption Committee’s welcome packages was not part
  of the vote. She realized when she read the minutes that this was included in the recommended
  action. Council Member Vasquez made a motion for reconsideration of the vote at the last
  meeting.

City Council Minutes  5  June 24, 2025
   Motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Mayor Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) hold a public
  discussion on the 2025-2027 Budget as necessary, conduct City Council deliberation,
  including allocation or reallocation of budgeted funds to adjust project details including
  timing. and (2) approve Resolution 25-26 Adopting the finally established Budget for the City
  of Mission Viejo for 2025-2027 and Appropriating Funds and approvals of process and
  commencement for the FY 2025/26 only items

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received written report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell reiterated that the planning code was updated to add the ability to build
vertically. He asked the Assistant City Manager to respond to the public speaker regarding the fuel
reduction contract. Assistant City Manager Hill commented that the apparent low bidder had an
incomplete bid, the second bidder did not possess both C27 and C49 licenses which were required
for this project. The bidder we awarded the contract to have both required licenses. Council Member
Goodell stated that he wanted to clarify this since it was inferred that there was favoritism when in
fact only one bidder was qualified to do the work, and they have done a great job in our city for a
long time.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley complimented the Mayor on the annual chamber breakfast stating it was
very well attended. She attended the Concert on Green on June 13 and expressed how fun these
concerts are, and it is a great event to take the whole family. She encouraged residents to attend the
next concert which will be in July. Council Member Kelley also attended the Night Market this past
weekend and encouraged residents to get there early to find a place to park. She reminded everyone
City Council Minutes  6  June 24, 2025
 about the 4th of July Street Faire which will start at noon. Lastly, she commented on the use of
goats for removal of brush and weeds for fire prevention and mentioned that the Transportation
Corridor Agency is using cattle and it has been very successful
Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez asked that in the future any agenda items relating to budgets that all of
the items going to be voted on be clarified before the vote. She also attended the Chamber breakfast
and had a nice time seeing familiar faces and meeting new people. She highlighted the Mission
Viejo Pride event this past weekend and estimated there were at least 2,000 people which doubled
from last year. There were ninety booths, several food trucks, the band Pulp Vixen and the Orange
County Gay Men’s Choral performed. She thanked all the fantastic sponsors. Council Member
Vasquez emphasized that it was very family friendly like any other Mission Viejo event only more
colorful. Dr. Stern of Saddleback College gave a very nice opening speech, and she said it was a
lovely even and she can’t wait to do it again next year.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum commented on the Chamber of Commerce Breakfast she attended and
gave kudos to Mayor Ruesch for his message of the State of the City. She highlighted her Father’s
Day Brunch at the Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club and mentioned that the golf club was built by Rancho
Mission Viejo and is owned by them. She stated that they have done incredible things in the
community such as during COVID they refused to take the City’s grant money and took care of
their own employees to make sure that they continued to be employed during that time. She said
she is proud of a business that thinks like that. Lastly, she announced that there is a lot going on
with Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) regarding the Olympics and
strategic planning. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum reported that Council Member Goodell may be asked
to speak to all the other cities and counties on what to do right relative to working with international
teams.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch attended the Rotary 50th Anniversary dinner at Casa Romantica and stated that the
City will be recognizing them in the near future. He attended the Mission Viejo Pride event this
past weekend along with his wife. Mayor Ruesch attended the OCFA Academy 61 graduation
ceremony and was honored to see a new recruit Edward Mendiola who happens to be the son-in-
law of one of our former Mayors Dave Leckness. He closed his comments with the following quote,
“The greatest gift you can give is your time, because when you give your time, you are giving a
portion of your life that you will never get back.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:10 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ruesch adjourned the meeting to Tuesday July 8, 2025, sending warm wishes and a speedy
recovery to 18-month-old Juliette Bryant who will be receiving a liver transplant tomorrow
morning.

City Council Minutes  7  June 24, 2025
 ______________________________________
Kimberly Shmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 8, 2025

City Council Minutes  8  June 24, 2025
